lg2 supports its own replacement syntax, so you don't need to use std::format.

Docs are here: https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-logging/blob/master/docs/structured-logging.md#lg2

This line, for example, would be:
```
lg2::info("Compatible system types found: {TYPES}", "TYPES", typesStr);
```

Same comment applies to other calls to lg2 in this file.
Done

I think you are going to get a duplicate replacement here. lg2 supports specifying exceptions as a replacement variable. And I would guess it just calls e.what(). So I think this can be simplified to:

```
lg2::error("Unable to load configuration file: {EXCEPTION}", "EXCEPTION", e);
```
Done

This is fine for now. But as more tests are written, I'd suggest putting the code that is used by both tests and the real executable into a static library. Then both can link with that library. See the phosphor-regulators or phosphor-power-sequencer executables/tests for an example.

I think this method of using inheritance to gain access to protected/private members is not recommended in the OpenBMC community.

I would suggest making public get methods for the data members that you need to inspect. For the methods that are not currently public, you could make them public or test them indirectly by calling a public method.

I think we still want to autotest as much of the code as we can. That means less manual testing, and it gets run thousands of times in the future. I'd rather not see your tests below get deleted.

While you cannot directly call findConfigFile, you can cause some/all of the variations by calling compatibleSystemTypesFound right?

If not, I think it is OK to make findConfigFile and/or loadConfigFile public. While we don't expect a user of this class to call them directly, it is also one of the main responsibilities of the class.
I can make it work with findConfigFile and loadConfigFile private, if I have a function to clear the compatible system types that is public.
Thanks for your changes. A few more comments.

It would be better if this was a `const std::vector<std::string>&`. Then it would not have to make a copy of the vector, which is somewhat expensive. By returning it as a const&, the caller cannot modify it (and mess up the Manager object).
